**On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s, night of March 13–14, 2026**

**Root cause**
Deploy `dep-4471` to the gateway, shipped by `a.novak` between 2:12 and 2:14 AM, flipped a config flag: `gateway.pool.perRequest` went from `false` to `true` (applied as config generation 119 at 2:13:41 AM). That change made every request grab its own database connection instead of sharing a pool. The pool only holds 20 connections, so it filled up almost immediately.

**Impact window**
First 503 hit at 2:14:18 AM, 37 seconds after the config change landed. The log runs out at 3:59:27 AM still showing failures, so as of the last recorded line the gateway had not recovered. That's at least 1 hour 45 minutes of impact, possibly ongoing.

Each failure shows the same pattern: a request fails with a 503 in 650 to 850 milliseconds, immediately followed by an `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED` error saying all 20 connections are in use. The backlog of stuck requests grew the whole time, from 13 waiting near the start to 74 waiting by 3:59 AM. In total, 530 requests failed this way, spread across `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/orders`, and `/v1/checkout`, hitting `billing-svc`, `orders-svc`, `catalog-svc`, and `accounts-svc` on the backend.

Background job workers were not affected. `logs/worker.log` covers the same night and shows zero errors.

**Rollback**
Roll back `dep-4471` on the gateway. Specifically, revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `true` back to `false`.
